ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r11.claim: He explains that the Prophet’s sight did not turn to either side.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما مال هكذا ولا هكذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r12.claim: He says the Prophet saw with certain, steady vision, neither turning away from the marvels shown nor exceeding what he was commanded to see.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r12.anchor: أي أثبت ما رآه إثباتا مستيقنا صحيحا من غير أن يزيغ بصره أو يتجاوزه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r13.claim: Another explanation says the Prophet’s sight stayed firmly on the object seen and did not go beyond it, confirming the event and dispelling doubt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13#2/r13.anchor: وما طغى: ولا تجاوز المرئي إلى غيره، بل وقع عليه وقوعا صحيحا

QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r1.claim: The Prophet's sight did not turn from the signs he was permitted to view or exceed its bounds; he observed the proper etiquette of the divine presence.
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r1.anchor: ببصره عما أبيح له من النظر إلى الآيات

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:16-20/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:16-20/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:16-20/r3.claim: The Prophet’s gaze neither deviated from what he saw nor exceeded it; he fixed it accurately and with certainty.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:16-20/r3.anchor: ما مال بصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عما رآه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:16-20/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:16-20/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:16-20/r4.claim: Alternatively, his gaze did not turn from the wonders he was commanded to see or go beyond them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:16-20/r4.anchor: أو ما عدل عن رؤية العجائب التي أمر برؤيتها وما جاوزها

FARRA:v3p97/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p97/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p97/r1.claim: The Prophet’s sight did not turn left or right, overstep, or exceed what he saw.
FARRA:v3p97/r1.anchor: بصر محمد صلى الله عليه ما زاغ بقلبه يمينا وشمالا ولا طغى ولا جاوز ما رأى

MAJAZ:v2p236/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p236/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p236/r1.claim: Mā zāgha al-baṣar means the sight did not deviate or stray.

MUQATIL:53:16-22/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:16-22/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:16-22/r1.claim: Muhammad's sight did not swerve or transgress; he did not wrong what he saw that night.
MUQATIL:53:16-22/r1.anchor: { ما زاغ البصر } يعني بصر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يعني ما مال { وما طغى } [آية: 17] يعني وما ظلم

NAHHAS:v4p270/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p270/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p270/r13.claim: ما زاغ means he did not veer right or left in confusion; وما طغى means he did not go beyond what he could discern.
NAHHAS:v4p270/r13.anchor: أي ما حاد يمينا وشمالا متحيرا ( وما طغى ) أي وما تجاوز

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.claim: Verses 13–18 refer to the Ascension and may belong to a later period than the early Makkan setting.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.anchor: Vv. 13–18, which refer to the Ascension of the Prophet, may, however, be from a later period

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.claim: Many commentators date the Ascension to the late Makkan period, most likely 619.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.anchor:
many commentators maintain that the Ascension of the Prophet Muhammad (miʿrāj
) did not occur until the late Makkan period, most likely in the year 619

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.speaker: a minority
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.claim: A minority dates the Ascension to 614, seven years before the hijrah.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.anchor: a minority maintain that it occurred seven years before the hijrah in 614

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.claim: The opening responds to the disbelievers’ claim in 52:33 that the Prophet invented the revelation.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.anchor: the opening verses respond to the contention of the disbelievers in 52:33, He has invented it

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.claim: The sūrah is famous for its rhetorical power and the dispute over the meaning of its opening section.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.anchor: because of its poetic rhetorical power and the debate that arises

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.claim: Many commentators identify the passage as the Prophet’s two visions of Gabriel in his true form, unlike Gabriel’s usual human appearance.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.anchor: Many commentators say the passage refers to the Prophet’s two visions of the Archangel Gabriel in his true form

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.speaker: many others
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.claim: Many others read the passage as the Prophet seeing God, by heart alone or by both eye and heart, during the Night Journey and Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.anchor: Many others interpret it as a reference to the Prophet’s vision of God

ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r1.claim: The Prophet’s sight neither deviated nor exceeded its proper course when he saw Gabriel filling the horizon.
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r1.anchor: ما عدل ولا جاوز القصد في رؤيته جبريل قد ملأ الأفق

RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r1.claim: The definite article may identify Muhammad’s sight: if locusts and moths covered the Sidra, he did not turn to them or lose sight of his purpose; their covering the tree tests him.
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r1.anchor: المعروف وهو بصر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r2.claim: If divine lights covered the Sidra, Muhammad neither looked aside nor became unconscious, unlike Moses; the readings display his composure and strength.

RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the article is generic: no sight at all veered under the awe. Rāzī answers that generic scope can also be expressed by a definite noun under negation, as in 6:103.

RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r4.claim: Mentioning sight rather than heart shows that the encounter was immense while Muhammad’s sight remained steady without involuntary deviation, like a composed person before a king.
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r4.anchor: يحصل منه فائدة أن الأمر كان عظيما

RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r5.claim: The clause may be an independent sentence or have an omitted subject supplied from the first clause.

RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r6.claim: With locusts or moths, Muhammad looked neither at them nor at anything besides God; with divine lights, he neither turned from the lights nor sought beyond them.
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r6.anchor: ولا إلى غير الجراد سوى الله

RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r7.claim: The word choice “deviate” and “transgress” marks looking aside or beyond as blameworthy in that setting; it also portrays Muhammad’s arrival at unsurpassed certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r7.anchor: الميل في ذلك الموضع والمجاوزة مذمومان

RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r8.claim: Rāzī also reads the sight as neither straying from the way nor perceiving things contrary to their reality, nor imagining something nonexistent as real.
RAZI-FULL:v28p253#2/r8.anchor: فلم ير الشيء على خلاف ما هو عليه

STUDYQURAN:53:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r1.claim: The Prophet’s gaze did not turn away from the wonders being revealed to him.
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r1.anchor: The Prophet’s gaze did not swerve from the wonders being revealed to him (Aj).

STUDYQURAN:53:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r2.speaker: Ṭū
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r2.claim: More generally, the verse means the Prophet did not turn away from the truth he sought.
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r2.anchor: More generally, it implies that he did not swerve away from the truth that he sought (Ṭū).

STUDYQURAN:53:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r3.speaker: Ṭū
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r3.claim: He did not seek anything beyond what was disclosed, whether the vision was of Gabriel or God.
STUDYQURAN:53:17/r3.anchor: Nor did it transgress then means that he did not seek anything beyond what was disclosed to him (Ṭū), whether it was the vision of Gabriel or the vision of God.

BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r1.claim: Zaygh means deviation from uprightness; the Prophet's sight did not turn even slightly away from what he saw.
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r1.anchor: الزيغ الميل عن الاستقامة أي ما مال بصر رسول الله عليه السلام أدنى ميل عما رآه

BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r2.claim: He neither exceeded bounds amid overwhelming sights, but retained them accurately, nor turned from the marvels he was enabled and commanded to see.
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r2.anchor: وما تجاوز مع ما شاهد هناك من الأمور المذهلة مما لا يحصى بل أثبته إثباتا صحيحا متيقنا

BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r3.claim: The author's preferred inference is that the Prophet saw God with physical eyesight while awake: describing the eye as steady indicates waking vision, whereas a heart-vision would mention the heart.
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r3.anchor: واستدل على أن رؤية الله كانت بعين بصره عليه السلام يقظة بقوله ما زاغ البصر

BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r4.claim: The alternative that baṣar means inner sight is possible in isolation, but the author rejects it because the passage supplies no contextual evidence for that reading.
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r4.anchor: وأمال القول بأنه يجوز أن يكون المراد بالبصر بصر قلبه

BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r5.claim: Al-Kashifi says Muhammad's eye neither turned aside nor exceeded its permitted bounds; this praises his good etiquette and high aspiration, as he looked only toward the everlasting divine beauty.
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي في معنى الآية : ميل نكرد شم محمد عليه السلام وي وراست ننكريست ودرنكذشت

BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r6.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads this as the Prophet's total poverty of self: his bodily sight ignored worldly attractions, his spiritual sight ignored afterlife rewards, and both attended wholly to God, His names, attributes, and manifestations.
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r6.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية يشير إلى تحقق النبي عليه السلام بمقام حقيقة الفقر الكلي الذي هو الخلو المطلق عما سواه

BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r7.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r7.claim: Al-Baqli applies the verse to the second vision: the first had nothing besides God, while this one shows the beloved's complete steadiness and desire to behold his Lord without turning even toward a noble thing.
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r7.anchor: وقال البقلي رحمه الله : هذه الآية في الرؤية الثانية لأن في الرؤية الأولى لم يكن شيء دون الله

BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r8.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r8.claim: Kashf al-Asrār contrasts Moses, who asked to see God and received 'You will not see Me' before repenting, with Muhammad, whose gaze was divinely guarded and praised as unwavering.
BURSEVI:v9p187#2/r8.anchor: وفي كشف الأسرار موسى عليه السلام ون ديدار خواست كه أرني أنظر إليك اورا بصمصام غيرت لن تراني جواب دادند

TABATABAI:53:17-18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:17-18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:17-18/r1.claim: The passage does not say the object seen was God; it names the upper horizon, nearness, and revelation, while the later verse calls what was seen God's great signs.
TABATABAI:53:17-18/r1.anchor: بل المرئي هو الأفق الأعلى والدنو والتدلي

TABATABAI:53:17-18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:17-18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:17-18/r3.claim: Even if the verse meant that the Prophet saw God, it would be heart-sight, unlike sensory eye-sight of bodies, and could relate to God.
TABATABAI:53:17-18/r3.anchor: فإنها رؤية القلب ورؤية القلب غير رؤية البصر الحسية

TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r6.claim: Zaygh is deviation from uprightness and, for sight, inaccurate perception; tughyān is exceeding a limit and, for sight, perceiving what is unreal.
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r6.anchor: الزيغ الميل عن الاستقامة، والطغيان تجاوز الحد في العمل

TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r7.claim: The sight in this verse is the Prophet's.
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r7.anchor: والمراد بالبصر بصر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r8.claim: The Prophet neither saw the object inaccurately nor saw anything unreal; he perceived without error.
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r8.anchor: لم يبصر ما أبصره على غير صفته الحقيقية

TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r9.claim: This seeing is the Prophet's heart-vision, the same kind of vision as the sighting at the other descent.
TABATABAI:53:17-18#2/r9.anchor: والمراد بالإبصار رؤيته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بقلبه لا بجارحة العين

TABRISI:53:14-18/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:14-18/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:14-18/r17.claim: The Prophet's sight did not turn aside or exceed its appointed limit; this praises his decorum at that station.
TABRISI:53:14-18/r17.anchor: ما زاغ بصر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يمل يمينا ولا شمالا وما طغى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r1.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns Muhammad, whom God strengthened to look at the signs without turning away in fear or panic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-؛ لأن الله تعالى أعطاه من القوة ما قوي به على النظر إلى الآيات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Muslim, says the gaze did not shift right or left or go beyond what Muhammad was commanded to see; al-Kalbi, Mujahid, and the exegetes agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r2.anchor: وروى مسلم عن ابن عباس: ما زاغ البصر يمينا ولا شمالا ولا جاوز ما أمر به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r3.claim: On this reading the verse praises Muhammad's decorum: he neither glanced aside nor stretched his gaze beyond the signs and wonders shown him; zaygh is a sideways glance and tughyan an overextended gaze.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p34/r3.anchor: فمعنى زيغ البصر: التفاته من الجانبين وطغيانه أنه يمد بصره أمامه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:14-17/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:14-17/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:14-17/r5.claim: This describes Muhammad's proper conduct during the Night Journey: his gaze did not turn from its appointed object or exceed what he was permitted.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:14-17/r5.anchor: هذا وصف أدب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة المعراج، أي: لم يمل بصره عما قصد له

QASHANI:53:16-18/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:16-18/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:16-18/r3.claim: His sight did not turn toward another or become occupied with seeing another.
QASHANI:53:16-18/r3.anchor: ما زاغ البصر } بالالتفات إلى الغير ورؤيته { وما طغى

QASHANI:53:16-18/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:16-18/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:16-18/r4.claim: His sight did not overstep by turning toward himself or becoming veiled by selfhood.
QASHANI:53:16-18/r4.anchor: وما طغى } بالنظر إلى نفسه واحتجابه بالأنائية

ELMALILI:53:15-17/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r10.claim: The Prophet's gaze did not stray or glance askance despite the astonishing sights; this expresses his proper adab.
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r10.anchor: Göz şaşmadı onu gören Resûlullah’ın gözü kaymadı, şaşıp da sağa sola bir eğri bakmadı

ELMALILI:53:15-17/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r11.claim: His sight did not exceed its proper limit or see falsely; this expresses its strength and precise observation.
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r11.anchor: وَمَا طَغَىٰ} ve aşmadı görmek haddini tecavüz edip de yanlış bir görüş de görmedi.

ELMALILI:53:15-17/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r12.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r12.claim: Razi contrasts Muhammad's steadiness with Moses fainting when the mountain was leveled; the Sidra stood firm and Muhammad was not shaken.
ELMALILI:53:15-17/r12.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Mûsâ aleyhisselâm’a olduğu gibi olmadı, zira onda cebel düpedüz olmuş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.claim: The mysterious, vivid scene points to faith about what senses cannot reach and warns against straining reason beyond its limits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.anchor: duyularla algılanamayan, fizik âlemin ötesine taşan konularda imanın esas olduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.claim: The passage condemns pagan attempts to make divinity concrete through material or spiritual intermediaries and to ascribe godhood to beings besides God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.anchor: Allah’tan başka varlıklara tanrılık izâfe etme telakkisini mahkûm etme

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.claim: Although the sūra is early Meccan, these verses, especially 13–18, are generally understood as relating to the Miʿrāj near the end of the Meccan period.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.anchor: 13-18. âyetlerin, Mekke döneminin sonlarına doğru gerçekleştiği bilinen mi‘rac olayı ile ilgili olduğu kabul edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r47.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r47.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r47.claim: Despite dazzling, astonishing sights, the Prophet did not look away, lose himself, or lapse in etiquette; he observed attentively and made sound observations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r47.anchor: sağa-sola yönelmemiş, gördüğü olağan üstü şeylerin etkisiyle kendinden geçmemiş, edepte kusur etmemiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r48.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r48.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r48.claim: The first verb conveys the Prophet’s courtesy, while the second conveys the strength of his gaze.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r48.anchor: Burada kullanılan fiillerden ilki onun edebini ikincisi de bakışındaki gücü belirtme mânası taşır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r49.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r49.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r49.claim: Commentators compare this event with Moses’ request to see God: the mountain shattered and Moses fell unconscious, whereas the Sidra and Muhammad did not suffer such a reaction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r49.anchor: dağ dayanamayıp parçalandığı ve kendisi de bayılıp yere düştüğü halde bu olayda sidre ve Resûl-i Ekrem açısından böyle bir durumla karşılaşılmadığı

ITQAN:v3p147/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p147/r3.speaker: ابن أبي شهاب
ITQAN:v3p147/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Shihab explains the Prophet's description of his speech as comprehensive: many matters from earlier books are gathered into one or two expressions.
ITQAN:v3p147/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي شهاب في معنى حديث الشيخين

TUSTARI:53:17/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:53:17/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:53:17/r1.claim: The gaze did not turn toward the self or its own witnessing; wholly absorbed in its Lord, it witnessed the attributes manifested to it that secured its steadiness there.
TUSTARI:53:17/r1.anchor: ما مال إلى شواهد نفسه ولا إلى مشاهدتها، وإنما كان مشاهدا بكليته ربه تعالى

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428#5/r1.claim: Zāgha means to deviate or turn aside.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428#5/r2.claim: Ṭaghā means to increase, exceed, or go beyond the limit.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p56/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p56/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p56/r1.claim: Zaygh is deviation to either side; taghyan is exceeding the limit or looking beyond what is permitted.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p56/r1.anchor: زاغ من الزيغان وهو الذهاب يمينا وشمالا أما الطغيان فهو مجاوزة الحد والقدر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p56/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p56/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p56/r2.claim: During the Prophet's journey, his gaze neither wandered nor exceeded its assigned place despite the scene's pull, praising his restraint in heaven as on earth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p56/r2.anchor: في رحلته ما مال بصره ولا جاوز قدره بل وقف في المكان الذي خصص له

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.claim: Verses 1–18 establish that the recited Qur'an is not soothsaying or fortune-telling but was revealed to the Prophet by God's trusted, dependable angel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.anchor: not the work of a soothsayer or a fortune-teller

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.claim: The discourse presents every verse as true and inevitable, and rejects the idea that the Prophet's experiences of revelation and Gabriel are illusions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.anchor: All its verses are based on the truth and what is stated in them is inevitable

ALUSI-FULL:v27p51#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p51#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p51#2/r1.claim: The Prophet's gaze neither turned from what he saw nor exceeded it; he saw it truly and certainly.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p51#2/r1.anchor: ما مال بصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عما رآه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p51#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p51#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p51#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, his gaze neither left the commanded wonders nor went beyond what he was not commanded to see.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p51#2/r2.anchor: وما جاوزها إلى ما لم يؤمر برؤيته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p406#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p406#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p406#2/r1.claim: The Prophet's sight did not turn right or left and did not exceed what he saw.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p406#2/r1.anchor: أي: ما مال بصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يمينا ولا شمالا وما طغى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p406#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p406#2/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p406#2/r2.claim: Another view says he did not exceed what he was commanded, describing his decorum because he did not glance aside.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p406#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: ما جاوز ما أمر به وهذا وصف أدبه في ذلك المقام إذ لم يلتفت جانبا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r12.claim: The Prophet’s unsurpassed sight neither fell short of what he was permitted to see nor exceeded its bounds, maintaining just, chaste moderation amid the realm’s wonders.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r12.anchor: { ما زاغ } أي ما مال أدنى ميل { البصر } أي الذي لا بصر لمخلوق أكمل منه , فما قصر عن النظر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r1.claim: The Prophet’s pardon of his Meccan kin at the conquest echoes Joseph’s pardon of his brothers; the source quotes Joseph’s words as the model.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r1.anchor: لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم } ) 77

DURR-FULL:v7p650/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the Prophet's gaze did not turn to the right or left.
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ما زاغ البصر} قال: ما ذهب يمينا ولا شمالا

DURR-FULL:v7p650/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gaze did not go beyond what the Prophet had been commanded to see.
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ما زاغ البصر} قال: ما ذهب يمينا ولا شمالا {وما طغى} قال: ما جاوز ما أمر به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r6.claim: The Prophet saw Gabriel without his eyesight straying or exceeding what was described; this restates the sight in 53:13–18 and denies exaggeration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r6.anchor: وجملة { ما زاغ البصر وما طغى } معترضة وهي في معنى جملة { ولقد رءاه نزلة أخرى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r7.claim: Zaygh is deviation from the intended course; the Prophet's sight did not turn to another object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r7.anchor: والزيع : الميل عن القصد ، أي ما مال بصره إلى مرئي آخر غير ما ذكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that the Prophet’s gaze did not wander to one side or the other.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس معناه: ما جال هكذا ولا هكذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r3.claim: The gaze did not go past the object seen; it met it accurately, confirming the event and eliminating doubt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r3.anchor: وما طغى معناه: ولا تجاوز المرئي، بل وقع عليه وقوعا صحيحا، وهذا تحقيق للأمر ونفي لوجود الريب عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p70#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p70#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p70#2/r1.claim: The Prophet’s gaze did not turn right or left or exceed what he saw; this describes his good conduct in that setting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p70#2/r1.anchor: أي ما عدل بصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يمينا ولا شمالا وما طغى أي ما زاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the gaze did not turn right or left and did not go beyond what it was commanded.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما ذهب يمينا ولا شمالا {وما طغى} ما جاوز ما أمر به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir sees the verse as praise for steadfast obedience: the Prophet did only what he was commanded and asked for nothing beyond what he was given.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r3.anchor: وهذه صفة عظيمة في الثبات والطاعة، فإنه ما فعل إلا ما أمر به، ولا سأل فوق ما أعطي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r4.speaker: الناظم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r4.claim: The cited poet says the Prophet saw the Garden of Abode and what lay above it; had he seen anything else, he would have been bewildered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r4.anchor: رأى جنة المأوى وما فوقها، ولو … رأى غيره ما قد رآه لتاها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود (على ظن محمد)
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.claim: A report tentatively attributed to Ibn Masud says Muhammad saw Gabriel in his form twice: once when requested, when Gabriel filled the horizon, and again on the ascent. Gabriel then returned to his form and prostrated; the great signs were Gabriel's creation. Ahmad transmits it and Ibn Kathir calls it strange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.anchor: قال محمد: أظنه عن ابن مسعود -أنه قال: إن محمدا لم ير جبريل في صورته إلا مرتين

JISHUMI:v9p6640/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r13.claim: Zaygh is turning aside from the sought truth.
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r13.anchor: والزيغ: الميل والذهاب عن الحق المطلوب، يقال: زاغ بصره وقلبه، يزيغ زيغا

JISHUMI:v9p6640/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r14.claim: Ṭughyān is seeking unjust elevation over another; ṭāghī parallels bāghī.
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r14.anchor: والطغيان: طلب العلو بظلم غيره، طغى طغيانا، والطاغي مثل الباغي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r20.claim: Zaygh of sight may mean deviation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r21.claim: Zaygh may mean that the sight went away.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r23.claim: Tughyan of sight may mean rising above the truth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r23.anchor: أحدها : ارتفاعه عن الحق . الثاني : تجاوزه للحق

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r24.claim: Tughyan may mean going beyond the truth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r24.anchor: الثاني : تجاوزه للحق ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r26.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r26.claim: Ibn Bahr concludes Muhammad saw accurately and truly, without deficient comprehension or excess imagined in his perception.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r26.anchor: من غير نقصان عجز عن إدراكه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#4/r1.claim: The Messenger's sight did not turn away from the marvels he was permitted to see.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#4/r1.anchor: بصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما عدل عن رؤية العجائب التى مر برؤيتها ومكن منها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#4/r2.claim: His sight did not go beyond what he was commanded to see.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ وما طغى ﴾ وما جاوز ما امر برؤيته

QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the gaze neither turned right or left nor exceeded the bounds of what it saw.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي ما عدل يمينا ولا شمالا، ولا تجاوز الحد الذي رأى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r5.claim: Other explanations are that Muḥammad did not exceed what he was commanded or extend his gaze to anything beyond the signs shown him.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r5.anchor: وقيل: ما جاوز ما أمر به. وقيل: لم يمد بصره إلى غير ما رأى من الآيات

QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r6.claim: The verse praises the Prophet’s decorum at that station: he did not look right or left.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:17-18/r6.anchor: وهذا وصف أدب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ذلك المقام إذ لم يلتفت يمينا ولا شمالا
